requirements.title: Instructor assessment of preparation
requirements.summary: Each instructor may determine whether a student is prepared to enter or continue the subject, subject to nondiscrimination and grievance rules. The source does not expressly waive course major restrictions; preparedness discretion is not recorded as blanket AI-major permission.

requirements.title: Prerequisite checking and course approval
requirements.summary: Prerequisites appear in GOLDcourse information and are checked at registration and again before the quarter; students who do not meet them are dropped. Instructor approval and a course approval code permit adds after the fifth instructional day through the add deadline; the page does not say that such a late-add code overrides a major restriction.

requirements.title: Conditional undergraduate graduate-course registration
requirements.summary: The optional graduate-course route typically serves exceptionally qualified seniors: cumulative GPA3.0and12upper-division units in the relevant major atB or better, with course instructor and offering-department chair approval; Creative Studies students also need their college dean. Eligible numbers are200–299and500-level GroupStudies/SpecialTopics; other500-level courses are unavailable. The stated300–499bachelor-credit prohibition is specifically LettersandScience, so it is not generalized to Engineering.

requirements.title: Quarterly enrollment completion and study load
requirements.summary: Quarterly registration, fee payment and removal of blocks must be completed by applicable deadlines. Register at least one course and resolve blocks by the15thinstructional day to avoid lapsed enrollment. Undergraduate full-time minimum12units; Engineering/LettersandScience maximum21units in good standing or17on probation. These are quarterly enrollment limits, not extra degree credits; late/retroactive enrollment and late course changes follow the published college processes.

requirements.title: Current general-subject scope and catalog cutoff
requirements.summary: General-area definitions and course lists apply to both Engineering and Letters and Science, but each college supplies its required counts. Areas B and C are expressly Letters and Science only. Additional approvals after the catalog cutoff may appear in GOLD; this is a published-catalog snapshot, not a live registration guarantee. The general page’s Engineering Area A2 list omits Writing105AI and the explicit online W variants included by the current Engineering-specific page; preserve that source-list difference rather than infer an exclusion or identity equivalence.

requirements.title: Certified IGETC and Cal-GETC routes
requirements.summary: The current university GE policy applies to all undergraduate colleges and expressly links Engineering. California community-college transfers with IGETC or Cal-GETC fully completed before matriculation and certified by the college satisfy the GE program. Partial certification may qualify when no more than two courses are lacking; the source literally names IGETC areas1–6 while discussing both patterns, so the receiving college determines completion of the partial program. The separate IGETC-for-STEM route permits at most three missing courses, one each in areas3,4,6, with certification and college consultation. Do not extend this STEM clause to Cal-GETC or infer a waiver of major or other university requirements.

requirements.title: Engineering special designations and petition scope
requirements.summary: Within the general-area courses, Engineering requires four designated writing courses, one ethnicity course, and one course in either European Traditions or World Cultures. Quantitative Relationships is Letters and Science only. Writing entails at least1800 non-exam words and substantial assessment weight. The special page’s permission to petition up to two other UCSB courses is expressly Letters and Science only, not an Engineering substitution rule; Engineering’s separately reviewed UCEAP petition exception remains distinct. Special designations overlay general areas rather than add seven disjoint courses.

ge-provisions.heading: General Provisions Governing All Degree Candidates

requirements.title: General-area nonreuse and permitted overlaps
requirements.summary: For Engineering and Letters and Science, a major course may also satisfy GE, and a GE course may simultaneously satisfy American History and Institutions. A course bearing multiple general-area designations A–G may apply to only one such area. Multiple listed memberships therefore represent alternatives, not permission to count one course in two general areas.

requirements.title: Current Engineering GE distribution and published lists
requirements.summary: Engineering requires six courses across D/E/F/G: at least two D, two E, one F and one G. Four writing, one ethnicity and one European Traditions-or-World Cultures designation are overlays within GE. The page links the current filtered course catalog as the approved-list source. Its Area A list expressly includes Writing105AI and W105M/W107B/W107L/W107WC/W109ST; the broader general-area page’s Engineering-only list does not repeat those entries. Existing writing-option inventory is therefore still under exact-version/list reconciliation. Certified transfer alternatives and no-double-use across general areas are recorded separately.
